concepts: pixel erosion, droplet nucleation, gravity-driven translation, static background retention, mass conservation
description: In the input you will see a centered white ice-cream scoop atop a brown waffle cone on a light-gray background, with some light-blue droplet pixels hanging beneath already. To produce the output, simulate one melting timestep: 1. Erode the scoop by removing a one-pixel-thick layer along its lower curved edge (smooth any jagged corners). 2. For every scoop pixel removed, spawn a new light-blue droplet pixel directly below its original location. 3. Move each existing light-blue droplet pixel down by one cell if that cell is empty (gravity). 4. Keep the cone, background, and any scoop highlights unchanged. The total count of removed white pixels equals the total of newly spawned light-blue pixels (mass conservation).
visual_elements: single-scoop ice-cream cone (white scoop atop a brown waffle cone)
plain neutral background (light gray or off-white)
dripping liquid forming small droplets beneath the scoop
subtle highlights and shadows on the scoop and cone
static_patterns: overall framing and camera angle remain fixed
size and shape of the waffle-cone pattern
position of the scoop relative to the cone
outline of the ice-cream scoop remains visible even as it melts
dynamic_patterns: scoop surface gradually shrinks and deforms
liquid drips form at scoop’s lower edge and fall downward
drips elongate, detach, and accelerate under gravity
remaining scoop surface smooths out as volume decreases
new droplets repeatedly nucleate at the melting front
core_principles: heat transfer causing phase change from solid (ice-cream) to liquid
gravity accelerating droplets downward once they detach
surface tension driving droplet formation and pinching off
mass conservation (scoop volume loss corresponds to total drip volume)
Summary: heat-induced melting under gravity leads to steady droplet formation and fall.
